title: Why food goes off more slowly in the cold
examples: Why does milk last longer in the fridge?
What is the food danger zone?

explain.say: Why does milk stay fresh for days in the fridge, but turn sour in hours on a hot day? Look at the curve. It shows how fast tiny living germs called bacteria grow at different temperatures. See the peak?

draw.text: Why food goes off more slowly in the cold

explain.say: The peak is near 37 degrees, the warmth of your body. Many bacteria love it there, and some can split in two every 20 minutes! One becomes two, two become four. Can you work out how many there are after one hour?

Yes, eight! Now look at the fridge mark, about 4 degrees. In the cold, bacteria slow right down, like you on a freezing morning. They still grow, just very slowly, so food lasts days instead of hours. That's why fridges are kept below 5 degrees.

See the freezer mark, minus 18 degrees? There, bacteria stop growing almost completely. At the other end, the cooking mark, heat above about 70 degrees kills most of them. So which part of the curve is the danger zone?

Exactly, the warm middle, from about 5 to 60 degrees! Brilliant. That's why leftovers go in the fridge within about two hours. Wow: before fridges, people in Nigeria and Sudan kept food cool in a zeer, a clay pot inside a pot of wet sand!

faq.q: Why does cold food go off more slowly?
faq.a: Food goes off mostly because bacteria and moulds grow on it. Cold slows them down a lot, so they take much longer to spoil the food.
asks: Why do we keep food in the fridge?

faq.q: What is the danger zone for food?
faq.a: Roughly 5 to 60 degrees Celsius, where bacteria grow fastest. Food safety guides say to keep food out of this range as much as possible.
asks: What temperature do bacteria grow fastest?

faq.a: No. Cold only slows bacteria down. When food warms up again, they start growing again.
asks: Do germs die in the fridge?

faq.a: In warm conditions, some bacteria can split in two about every 20 minutes. So one cell can become millions in a few hours.

faq.q: How did people keep food cool before fridges?
faq.a: They used cold cellars, ice cut from frozen lakes, and clay pot coolers like the zeer, used in Nigeria and Sudan, where water evaporating from wet sand cools the inner pot.

facts: Food safety agencies advise keeping fridges at or below about 5 °C.
Freezing at −18 °C stops bacteria from multiplying but does not kill most of them.

quiz.say: At which temperature do many germs grow fastest?
quiz.show: At which temperature do many germs grow fastest?
quiz.why: Many bacteria grow fastest near body temperature.

wrong.1: 4 °C is fridge temperature, where bacteria grow very slowly.
wrong.2: −18 °C is freezer temperature, where growth almost stops.

quiz.say: What does a fridge do to bacteria?
quiz.show: What does a fridge do to bacteria?
quiz.why: Cold slows bacteria but does not kill them.

wrong.1: Cold doesn't kill most bacteria; cooking does.
wrong.2: Cold makes them grow slower, not faster.
